'''Kevin Maurice Garnett''' ({{IPAc-en|g|ɑːr|ˈ|n|ɛ|t}} {{respell|gar-NET}}; born May 19, 1976), commonly known by his initials '''KG''', is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 21 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed "'''the Big Ticket'''", Garnett is widely regarded as one of the greatest [[Power forward (basketball)|power forwards]] of all time, known for his intensity, versatility, and defensive ability.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/nba/gallery/ranking-the-25-greatest-players-in-nba-history-100716 |title=Ranking the 25 greatest players in NBA history |work=FOX Sports |date=October 20, 2017 |access-date=March 7, 2019}}</ref> As of 2026, he is one of five NBA players to have won both the [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award]] and the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award]].{{refn|group="n"|[[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]], [[Michael Jordan]], [[Hakeem Olajuwon]], and [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] are the other four.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/giannis-antetokounmpo-of-the-milwaukee-bucks-named-2019-20-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year/wthcjku50icu1k4iv9sbuq3ku |title=Giannis Antetokounmpo of the Milwaukee Bucks named 2019-20 NBA Defensive Player of the Year |last=Rafferty |first=Scott |work=ca.nba.com |date=August 25, 2020 |access-date=September 18, 2021}}</ref>}}

In high school, Garnett was a [[1995 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|1995]] [[McDonald's All-American]] at [[Farragut Career Academy]] and a national player of the year award winner.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2010/columns/story?page=beforetheywerestars-garnett-100608 |title=Before they were stars: Boston Celtics' Kevin Garnett |work=ESPN |date=June 8, 2010 |access-date=December 29, 2010}}</ref><ref name=mcdonalds>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/wilkins-honored-one-35-greatest-mcdonalds-all-americans |title=Wilkins Honored as One of 35 Greatest McDonald's All Americans |publisher=NBA |date=January 31, 2012 |access-date=February 9, 2012}}</ref> He entered the [[1995 NBA draft]], where he was selected with the fifth overall pick by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and became the first NBA player drafted [[NBA high school draftees|directly out of high school]] in [[1975 NBA draft|20 years]]. Garnett made an immediate impact with the Minnesota Timberwolves, leading them to eight consecutive [[NBA Playoffs|playoff]] appearances. In 2004, he led the Timberwolves to the [[NBA Conference Finals|Western Conference Finals]] and won the NBA MVP Award. He was named the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] with the [[Boston Celtics]] during the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], his first with the team.

Garnett was traded to the Celtics in 2007, helping guide them to the [[2008 NBA Finals]] and beat the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], while also finishing in third place for the [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] award.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/kobe_mvp_080506.html |title=NBA.com - Kobe Bryant Wins Most Valuable Player Award<!-- Bot generated title --> |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=May 30, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401110138/http://www.nba.com/news/kobe_mvp_080506.html |archive-date=April 1, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2013, Garnett was included in a second headline trade that sent him to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] with longtime Celtic [[Paul Pierce]]. In 2015, Garnett was traded back to Minnesota. He announced his retirement from professional basketball in September 2016. He was inducted into the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] in 2020 and named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]] in 2021.

During his NBA career, Garnett was named to 15 [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]]s, winning the [[NBA All-Star Game Most Valuable Player Award|All-Star MVP award]] in [[2003 NBA All-Star Game|2003]].{{refn|group="n"|Garnett is tied with [[Shaquille O'Neal]] and [[Tim Duncan]] for the fourth-most All-Star selections of all time. They trail [[Kobe Bryant]] (17 selections), [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]], and [[LeBron James]] (19 each).}} He was named to the [[All-NBA Team]] nine times and the [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] 12 times.<ref name="stats">{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/garneke01.html |title=Kevin Garnett Statistics |work=Basketball-reference.com |access-date=October 27, 2008}}</ref> Garnett also holds several Timberwolves [[Franchise player|franchise]] records.

Garnett made his feature film debut in the 2019 crime thriller ''[[Uncut Gems]]'', playing a fictionalized version of himself.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chaudhary |first=Aikansh |date=September 23, 2020 |title=NBA Hall of Famer Kevin Garnett Has an Interesting Take on Why Bubble Wouldn't Work for His Generation of Players |url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nba-news-nba-hall-of-famer-kevin-garnett-has-an-interesting-take-on-why-bubble-wouldnt-work-for-his-generation-of-players/ |access-date=November 2, 2020 |website=EssentiallySports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ciccotelli |first=Jenna |title=Kevin Garnett Explains Why His Generation 'Could Never' Play in an NBA Bubble |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2910273-kevin-garnett-explains-why-his-generation-could-never-play-in-an-nba-bubble |access-date=November 2, 2020 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>

As a college basketball player, Van Horn played for the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]] for four seasons. The Utes won the WAC Tournament twice and reached the NCAA Tournament three times during Van Horn's collegiate career. Van Horn was a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in 1996 and a consensus first-team All-American in 1997. As a senior in 1997, he was named ESPN Men's College Basketball Player of the Year. Van Horn finished his [[college basketball]] career with the Utes as the all-time leading scorer in the history of the [[Western Athletic Conference]] (WAC). Van Horn was selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the second pick in the 1997 NBA draft and was traded to the [[New Jersey Nets]] on draft night. He was named to the 1998 NBA All-Rookie Team. Van Horn played for the Nets from 1997 to 2002, leading the team in scoring in the 1997–98 and 1998–99 seasons and finishing fifth in the NBA in scoring with 21.8 points per game in the 1998–99 season. He was a member of the 2001–02 Nets team that made the NBA Finals. Van Horn would also go on to play for the 76ers, the [[New York Knicks]], the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], and the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He averaged 16 points and nearly seven rebounds per game during his NBA career.

'''Kenneth Alexander Satterfield''' (born April 10, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played college basketball for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]] beginning in 1999. In 2001, after a successful sophomore season, he bolted for the NBA, being drafted 53rd overall (second round) by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[2001 NBA draft]]. He played for the [[Denver Nuggets]] (2001–2002) and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] (December 2002 – 2003).

During his time with the Nuggets, he coined the nickname "Birdman" for teammate [[Chris Andersen]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130708070803/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1160761 Flight Of The Birdman]</ref>

Satterfield posted NBA career averages of 4.3 points, 1.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists in a total of 75 games. Coincidentally, Satterfield's final NBA game ever was also his homecoming game against the Denver Nuggets. After leaving the Nuggets and joining the 76ers, his very first game against Denver at the Pepsi Center (Denver's arena) was on March 2, 2003, which ended up being his last game in the league. Philadelphia won the game 100 - 94 with Satterfield recording 2 assists but no points.

Satterfield a.k.a. "Serious Satellite" is also a well known [[streetball]] player on the basketball courts of the [[New York City]] summer leagues.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/item_qx3PuIo6XuvjxhuTecFPVO;jsessionid=10693C4B02BAC27455EDC65BE7176E73|title=POINT TAKEN}}{{Dead link|date=May 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

After his NBA venture, Satterfield had a stint with the now defunct [[NBA G League|NBDL]]'s [[Fayetteville Patriots]]. He also played abroad<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/players/kenny_satterfield.htm/|title=NBA Players}}</ref> in [[LNB Pro A|France]], [[A1 Ethniki|Greece]], [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto (Venezuela)|Venezuela]] and [[Lebanon]], with [[Al Hikmeh Sagesse]] (in 2005–06), which he left in early 2006 without notice, and Riyadi Beirut.

In 2010, he played for the [[Albany Legends]] of the [[International Basketball League|IBL]]. On April 30, 2010, he achieved a triple-double with 13 points, 12 rebounds, and 13 assists in a 100–106 loss to the Tacoma Tide.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ibl.com/box_score.php?gameid=3676 |title=Tacoma Tide vs Albany Legends Box Score |access-date=May 23, 2013 |archive-date=July 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120729150340/http://www.ibl.com/box_score.php?gameid=3676 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On May 22, 2010, he put up 31 points and 18 assists in a 142–124 win over the [[Holland Blast]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ibl.com/box_score.php?gameid=3680 |title=Holland Blast vs Albany Legends Box Score |access-date=May 23, 2013 |archive-date=July 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120729150348/http://www.ibl.com/box_score.php?gameid=3680 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He finished the season leading the team in points and assists. The Legends went on to win the 2010 IBL Championship.

'''Kenyata Allen Johnson''' (born February 1, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A {{convert|6|ft|11|in|cm|adj=on}}, {{convert|240|lb|kg|adj=on|abbr=on}} [[Center (basketball)|center]], he played collegiately at [[Ohio State University]]. He played in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA), and the [[NBA Development League]]. He also played in France, in Italy, in Germany with [[Telekom Baskets Bonn]], in Estonia with [[BC Kalev/Cramo]] and in Spain with [[CB Atapuerca|Ford Burgos]].

Johnson was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] in the 2nd round of the [[2001 NBA draft]] with the 48th pick overall.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2001/news/draft_order.html |title=NBA Draft 2001 |work=nba.com |access-date=2011-01-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110210143314/http://www.nba.com/draft2001/news/draft_order.html |archive-date=2011-02-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played for the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) during the 2001–02 season and was selected to the CBA All-Defensive and All-Rookie Teams.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ken Johnson minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-johnsken001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=June 27, 2021}}</ref> He won a [[CBA champion]]ship with the Wizards in 2002.<ref>{{cite web |title=2001-02 Dakota Wizards Statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/t-DLGDAK/y-2001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=March 12, 2025}}</ref> He played 16 games of one NBA season ([[2002-03 NBA season|2002–03]]), averaging 2.0 points and 2.0 rebounds per game. Johnson's final NBA game was on April 15, 2003, in a 103–99 win over the Toronto Raptors where he came off the bench playing for 33 minutes and recorded 8 points, 10 rebounds, 1 steal and 1 block.

He was the first overall selection in the 2003 NBA Development League Draft.
